name: OIBench
intro: OIBench 是面向强推理模型的高难度信息学奥赛基准，固定论文与公开数据均包含250道由资深竞赛教练原创、发布前未公开的中英文题目。每题配有难度标签、大规模测试与经执行验证的C++标准解；主榜以四种编程语言的全测试通过率评估正确性，时间/空间完成曲线则使用逐测试用例通过率评估效率。
org: AGI-Eval, Beijing Normal University, Meituan, Shanghai Jiao Tong University
build_method: 资深OI教练原创命题, 原创性门禁, 标准解全测试验证, 六人复审, 专业双语翻译与联网查重
metric: 主榜：全部测试通过的AC率；效率曲线：相对标准解资源比例下的逐测试用例通过率（非AC）
task_type: 信息学奥赛, 竞赛编程, 代码效率
eval_feature: 原创抗污染, 四种编程语言, 全测试通过
scale: 250道原创双语题；固定HF revision 7736d476…为250行；含测试、难度标签与C++标准解
task_type_en: Olympiad in Informatics, competitive programming, code efficiency
build_method_en: Experienced-coach Original Authoring, Originality Gate, All-test Canonical-solution Verification, Six-person Review, Professional Translation and Retrieval Audit
eval_feature_en: Original Anti-contamination Data, Four Programming Languages, All-tests-correct
intro_en: OIBench is a high-difficulty Olympiad-in-Informatics benchmark for strong reasoning models. Both the pinned paper and public dataset contain 250 original Chinese and English problems authored by experienced contest coaches and kept private before release. Each problem includes difficulty tags, large official tests, and an execution-verified canonical C++ solution; the main leaderboard uses all-tests-correct acceptance in four programming languages, while time/space completion curves measure per-test-case progress.
scale_en: 250 original bilingual problems; pinned HF revision 7736d476… has 250 rows; includes tests, difficulty tags, and canonical C++ solutions
metric_en: Main table: all-tests-correct AC rate; efficiency curves: per-test-case pass rate at resource ratios relative to the canonical solution, not problem AC

drawio_review_note: Source-scoped audit reviewed 2026-07-18. The paper contract is pinned to arXiv:2506.10481v1 (the only paper version visible during review), whose downloaded PDF has SHA-256 42dc756e1ed2240446aca051fb8c356cbd1a6c5f592b1451af9618f7ec8a0d5a. Public implementation evidence is pinned to AGI-Eval-Official/OIBench commit 2a84ab8fd42b8827c8433691ebe9a7cd8ae12191 and the AGI-Eval/OIBench Hugging Face revision 7736d4769c84d9dcb4069c118865b5dd75bc5167, which exposes 250 rows and declares CC BY-ND 4.0. Paper Sections 3–5 and Appendices A.4 and A.9–A.10 describe the main construction flow. Coaches from university ACM and high-school OI teams average about 20 years of coaching experience and select problems from private repositories or author new ones. Problems must be unpublished online and in print; number-only or wording-only adaptations are rejected in favor of new underlying logic. Authors assign Codeforces-style difficulty and competition-level metadata, write large/resource-intensive/edge-focused official tests, and provide a canonical C++ solution for every problem. The body says those tests meet standards located in the Appendix, but arXiv v1 Appendix A.1–A.10 does not enumerate those test standards; the diagram records that disclosure gap instead of inventing criteria. Each canonical solution is executed against every official test to confirm solvability and test correctness. Six undergraduate computer-science OI participants with at least CCPC silver medals review solvability, clarity, samples, TeX, and Markdown. Three professional translators with translation degrees and at least two years of experience produce English statements using an OI glossary developed with coaches and contestants. Every problem is searched online; the paper freezes the no-direct-retrieval claim at May 2025. The resulting release contains 250 bilingual problems with statements, tags, level, canonical C++, official tests, pseudocode, buggy/corrupted variants, and human-participant records; the paper reports an average test size of 37.5M. For the main benchmark, models receive the full problem and OJ input/output format zero-shot and generate C++, Java, Python, or JavaScript with up to 32,768 reasoning tokens. Decoding is greedy at temperature 0 by default, while DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3-32B use temperature 0.6. The paper runtime is a fixed Docker environment: CentOS 7.6, Linux kernel 5.4, glibc 2.31, g++11.3 with C++17 -O2, Java 1.8.0_45, Node 16.18.1/npm 8.19.2, and Python 3.9. Main Table 3 AC accepts a problem only when every official test passes and reports overall, language, and Chinese-versus-English breakdowns. Time and Space Completion Curves are a separate efficiency view: their X-axis is the resource ratio to the canonical solution on a log scale, and their Y-axis is the fraction of individual test cases solved, not problem-level AC. OIBench Pseudo, Risk-Score contamination analysis, derived BF/CP/TS/IT tasks, and the 44-problem human comparison remain separate tracks and are not merged into the main AC flow. The pinned public scorer is not an exact executable copy of that paper environment: its README requests host toolchains including OpenJDK 11, code defaults to C++, applies a 10-second timeout and pass@k-shaped aggregation that effectively requires all cases for its single candidate, and contains no fixed Docker configuration or Time/Space Completion Curve implementation. The public code tree also has no LICENSE file, so the repository being readable must not be interpreted as a granted code license. The diagram therefore distinguishes the paper contract, public dataset license, and observed scorer behavior instead of silently treating them as identical. Formal publication evidence [site-a11y-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 4045×521 (English) and 4045×521 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 4043×519 and 4043×519. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
